Core aeration physically removes soil. Liquid aeration takes a different approach: a soil-conditioning treatment is applied across the turf to support better wetting and water movement over time. It gives homeowners a lower-disruption option for ongoing soil-health support.
It offers broad coverage with very little surface disruption, making it easy to add soil-health support to an established lawn-care plan.
Soil-conditioning ingredients are designed to help irrigation and rainfall spread through hard-to-wet areas more consistently.
The lawn keeps a clean appearance after treatment because no cores are pulled and left across the surface.
Tight gates, slopes, irrigation-heavy lawns and narrow turf sections can be covered without core-aerator access.
Liquid aeration fits naturally alongside fertilization, irrigation management and other long-term soil-health practices.
The lawn is treated evenly, there are no soil cores to clean up and we provide the watering and aftercare directions for that application.
We consider the turf, access, irrigation and the soil-health concerns behind your request before completing the application.
The liquid treatment is applied across the lawn without a core machine, open holes or piles of soil plugs.
We provide watering and re-entry guidance based on the application so the treatment can be used as intended.
The services are not identical. We would rather recommend the approach that matches the property than pretend one option is automatically best for every lawn.
You want ongoing soil-health support and broad treatment coverage without holes, plugs or mechanical aeration equipment.
The priority is immediate physical decompaction by removing soil plugs from a heavily trafficked or severely compacted lawn.
Not sure which one you need? Request the estimate and tell us what you are seeing. We can recommend liquid, core or neither based on the lawn instead of forcing the wrong service.

Soil-health services should support the lawn—not just sound impressive on a sales page. We work with South Louisiana warm-season turf and explain where liquid aeration fits, what to expect and when mechanical core aeration makes more sense.
Liquid aeration is a soil-conditioning application made across the turf. It is designed to support better wetting and water movement through the soil profile without mechanically removing soil cores.

It does not physically remove compacted soil the way hollow-tine core aeration does. Liquid aeration is better understood as gradual soil-conditioning and moisture-management support. Severe compaction may still call for core aeration .
No. A liquid application does not pull soil cores, so there are no aeration holes or plugs left across the surface. The lawn may simply look like it received a normal liquid treatment.

We use lawn-treatment programs across common South Louisiana warm-season turf, including St. Augustine, centipede, zoysia and bermuda. We will consider turf condition and timing before recommending the service.

Liquid aeration is not intended to create an instant color change. Response depends on soil conditions, weather, irrigation and the overall lawn program. Think of it as improving the growing environment over time rather than providing an overnight cosmetic result.
Watering may be part of the aftercare, but the amount and timing should come from your service instructions rather than a universal rule. We will tell you what to do after the application.

We apply professional products according to their directions. Follow the re-entry instructions provided after service and keep people and pets off the treated area until the stated interval has passed.

Pricing depends primarily on the amount of turf being treated, property access and site conditions. Send the address through the estimate form and our office can review the property and provide straightforward pricing.
Get a straightforward liquid aeration estimate—and an honest recommendation about whether it is the right fit for your South Louisiana lawn.

What the service actually does

Soil conditioning—not mechanical plug removal

Core aeration physically removes soil. Liquid aeration takes a different approach: a soil-conditioning treatment is applied across the turf to support better wetting and water movement over time. It gives homeowners a lower-disruption option for ongoing soil-health support.

  • It covers the treatment area uniformly. Tight corners and areas near irrigation can be treated without maneuvering a bulky aerator.
  • It leaves no cores on the surface. There are no temporary soil plugs to dry, crumble or mow back into the lawn.
  • It works below the surface. This is not instant green paint or a cosmetic treatment; benefits develop as soil moisture behavior and roots respond.
  • It does not physically remove compacted soil. When severe compaction needs immediate mechanical relief, core aeration may be the stronger recommendation.
A cleaner soil-health option

Why homeowners choose liquid aeration

It offers broad coverage with very little surface disruption, making it easy to add soil-health support to an established lawn-care plan.

Liquid aeration fits naturally alongside fertilization, irrigation management and other long-term soil-health practices.

  • Unlock gates and move toys, hoses, furniture and pet waste from the treatment area.
  • Let the office know about access restrictions, recent sod or areas you do not want treated.
  • You generally do not need to mark sprinkler heads solely to protect them from coring tines.

After we leave

  • Follow the watering directions in your service communication rather than using a one-size-fits-all amount.
  • Follow the provided people-and-pet re-entry instructions before using the treated lawn.
  • Expect gradual soil-health support—not an overnight cosmetic change in turf color.

  • A clean lawn appearance immediately after service matters

  • The ground is extremely hard or traffic-compacted
  • Physical soil removal is the main objective
  • A core machine can safely access the treatment area
  • You are comfortable marking obstacles and leaving temporary plugs

Why Grow Green

An honest recommendation from a company that specializes in lawns

Soil-health services should support the lawn—not just sound impressive on a sales page. We work with South Louisiana warm-season turf and explain where liquid aeration fits, what to expect and when mechanical core aeration makes more sense.

  • Local expertise: Recommendations built around St. Augustine, centipede, zoysia and bermuda lawns.
  • Clear expectations: Liquid aeration is positioned as gradual soil conditioning, not an overnight miracle.
  • Practical guidance: You receive the watering and re-entry directions that apply to your service.
  • No-pressure pricing: Review the estimate, ask questions and decide when it makes sense for your property.
Good to know

Liquid aeration questions we hear most

What is liquid aeration?

Liquid aeration is a soil-conditioning application made across the turf. It is designed to support better wetting and water movement through the soil profile without mechanically removing soil cores.

Does liquid aeration physically break apart compacted soil?

It does not physically remove compacted soil the way hollow-tine core aeration does. Liquid aeration is better understood as gradual soil-conditioning and moisture-management support. Severe compaction may still call for core aeration.

Will there be holes or plugs across my lawn?

No. A liquid application does not pull soil cores, so there are no aeration holes or plugs left across the surface. The lawn may simply look like it received a normal liquid treatment.

Is liquid aeration suitable for my grass type?

We use lawn-treatment programs across common South Louisiana warm-season turf, including St. Augustine, centipede, zoysia and bermuda. We will consider turf condition and timing before recommending the service.

How soon should I expect results?

Liquid aeration is not intended to create an instant color change. Response depends on soil conditions, weather, irrigation and the overall lawn program. Think of it as improving the growing environment over time rather than providing an overnight cosmetic result.

Do I need to water after liquid aeration?

Watering may be part of the aftercare, but the amount and timing should come from your service instructions rather than a universal rule. We will tell you what to do after the application.

Is liquid aeration safe around people and pets?

We apply professional products according to their directions. Follow the re-entry instructions provided after service and keep people and pets off the treated area until the stated interval has passed.

How is liquid aeration priced?

Pricing depends primarily on the amount of turf being treated, property access and site conditions. Send the address through the estimate form and our office can review the property and provide straightforward pricing.
